description:
Strongly-typed Avalonia theming. Decorate a class with [Theme], install this package, and the bundled Roslyn source generator emits one markup extension per public property, so your XAML binds theme values directly with full IntelliSense and no runtime code generation. Extensions sort into three namespaces by the property's C# type: {colour:...} for paint (Avalonia.Media.Color and anything implementing IBrush), {size:...} for measures (double/int/float/decimal, Thickness, CornerRadius, GridLength, Point, Size) and {theme:...} for everything else. Breaking change in 1.11.0: colour and size tokens moved out of {theme:...}; add the two xmlns and repoint those usages.

ACCENTS. {colour:AccentBrush} resolves against whichever hue the target control carries, so one accent style block serves every hue instead of a copy per accent. Callers write theme:Accent.Kind="Warning"; the hue inherits, so it reaches control template parts and a container tints everything beneath it. Hues and shades are inferred from the theme's own Color Accent{Hue} and Accent{Hue}{Shade}Brush properties, so adding a hue is a theme edit and nothing else: the enum, the XAML value and the IntelliSense follow. Hues added downstream are honoured by control styles compiled before they existed.

ACCENT ROLES. [AccentRole] on a property whose constant RampStage value pins a stage (e.g. internal virtual RampStage TextDefault => RampStage.Dark1) generates {colour:TextDefault} and {colour:TextDefaultBrush}, which resolve that stage against the target control's hue — a named token for recurring assignments like outlined text ink or rest fill, retunable globally from one property.

ICONS. Mark a class [IconGallery] and every public string property becomes an {icons:IconName} extension.

PREVIEW STATES. theme:Preview.State="Hover" makes a control paint an interaction state without being interacted with, so a gallery or a spec page can show hover, pressed and focused side by side. Pair it with the real pseudo-class in one selector: ^:pointerover, ^[(theme|Preview.State)=Hover]. Being an attached property rather than a style class, an IDE resolves it and a typo is a compile error.

SCOPED REGIONS. theme:ThemeRegion.Theme pins a full alternate theme to a subtree while the rest of the app keeps the global one, and theme:ThemeRegion.IsDark="True" mirrors whichever base is in effect into its dark ramp; both inherit, so a container retints everything beneath it down into template parts, and the sugar degrades gracefully to the unmirrored base when a theme cannot be cloned.

STYLE CLASSES. A bundled MSBuild target generates the stub declarations that stop IDEs underlining Classes="accent" on markup that works, keeping them in step with your ControlThemes automatically. Breaking change in 1.13.0: it is now opt-in via GenerateStyleClassDeclarations=true, and the file is generated in full rather than spliced between BEGIN/END markers. Prefer an attached property where you can — a class declared as ^.name inside a ControlTheme is invisible to static analysis, which is the whole reason the stub file has to exist.

Includes AngelSix.ThemeEngine.SourceGen as an analyzer; a single install gives you the runtime, the generator and the build targets.
